claim: Try it with sample data; demo settings stay separate, Reset demo removes them, and Start for real clears demo keys without changing real keys.
where: landing action, demo banner, privacy page, README
sandbox: fresh browser context at /demo/; save a sample pronunciation, assert only the demo namespace is used, reset it, then verify Start for real clears demo keys while preserving a real-data sentinel

claim: The demo reads a selection or current line and applies a personal pronunciation.
sandbox: fresh demo; select an identifier, set its pronunciation, then collapse the selection and verify current-line output

claim: Demo code stays in the browser.
sandbox: record every request while editing and listening to sample code; assert every request is same-origin

claim: Every shipped structural-cue fixture produces its expected spoken symbol or indentation label.
where: landing how-it-works section, extension descriptions, README
sandbox: run every shipped JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Rust, and shell fixture; assert every expected spoken cue appears in generated output

claim: The reader gives source only to a voice marked local; without one, the spoken preview remains and speech is blocked.
where: reader preview, privacy page, browser and VS Code packages, README
sandbox: fresh demo with only a non-local English voice; assert no utterance is constructed or spoken, the preview remains, and local-voice recovery is shown

claim: Works offline after the first visit.
where: landing facts and demo offline notice
sandbox: fresh browser context with a local speech mock; load /demo/, wait for service-worker control, disable network, reload, edit sample code, and assert the preview and one local speech call

claim: Landing preview changes are not saved and disappear after reload.
sandbox: fresh landing page; preview a pronunciation, assert no local-storage key is created, reload, and assert the shipped pronunciation is restored
fresh unauthenticated browser context downloads the packaged browser extension

claim: The installed browser popup saves language, punctuation, rate, indentation, and personal pronunciation settings.
sandbox: change each setting through the installed popup and inspect only extension-local storage

claim: Both extensions export and import the same versioned JSON pronunciation file without source code.
where: landing pronunciation section, browser popup, VS Code settings, README
test: npm run test:installed && npm run test:vscode-installed
sandbox: fresh packaged browser and VS Code harnesses export a map, preview a valid version 1 file, apply it locally, and assert the file contains word pairs but no editor source

claim: Browser extension shortcuts are configurable in the browser's extension shortcut settings.
sandbox: install the distributable ZIP in a fresh Chromium profile, change Listen to code from Alt+Shift+S to Alt+Shift+L on Chromium's extension shortcut settings page, invoke the new shortcut, then restore it

claim: The installed browser package stores reading settings locally, does not store source, and makes no remote request while listening.
sandbox: install the distributable ZIP in a fresh Chromium profile, listen to private sample source, inspect extension storage, and record HTTP(S) requests

claim: The packaged VS Code extension reads a selection or current line and supports follow, repeat, stop, and reading settings.
where: README and VS Code package description
sandbox: unpack the VSIX into a fresh host harness, activate it, invoke every command, and inspect the speech/settings messages

claim: The packaged VS Code extension keeps reading settings in local extension state and does not store or send source code.
sandbox: activate the packaged VSIX in an isolated host harness, save settings, inspect state, and fail any network request
